Package hadur2.core.policy

Class MoveFlavour

java.lang.Object
hadur2.core.policy.MoveFlavour
public final class MoveFlavour extends Object
MOVE-2: when the enemy hits us more than its profile says it does, beyond the margin of error, the movement changes flavour at the next surfable wave. Each change adds one more step, in MoveFlavour.Step's order, and then needs fresh evidence (a window started at the change) before the next: a gun that has learned the new movement too shows it again. With no profile there is no baseline, so a stranger never changes flavour (DIAL-1).

HadurCore makes one per opponent, with the profile's raw hit rate on us as the baseline, and calls onWave(boolean) for every enemy wave that breaks. When a step is returned it applies it through the movement's own setters (the flattener views, the surf's go-to mode, DistancePolicy.shiftOut(double)); this class only decides. After MoveFlavour.Step.FAR there is nothing left to add and the flavour stays where it is.

  • Field Details

    • MAX_MARGIN

      public static final double MAX_MARGIN
      DIAL-1: the live rate's margin must be at most this before it can change anything. Agresti-Coull is generous with a handful of waves (one hit in one wave already clears a 10% baseline), so a change waits for about 40 waves of evidence.

    • onWave

      public MoveFlavour.Step onWave(boolean hit)
      One enemy wave broke, a hit or a miss. Returns the step added, or null when the flavour stays.

      The outcome is always recorded, so live() keeps reporting. A change needs the live estimate to be certain enough (MAX_MARGIN) and certainly above the baseline (above(hadur2.core.memory.Estimate, hadur2.core.memory.Estimate)); it then moves one step on and clears the window, so the next change is judged only on waves against the new flavour.

      Parameters:
      hit - whether the wave's bullet hit us
      Returns:
      the step just added, or null for no change

    • above

      public static boolean above(Estimate live, Estimate baseline)
      DIAL-1: whether live exceeds baseline by more than the margin of error of the difference (both at their Agresti-Coull centres).

      As in DistancePolicy.certainLead(hadur2.core.memory.Estimate, hadur2.core.memory.Estimate), the margin of the difference of two independent estimates is the root of the sum of their squared margins. Either rate unknown means no.

      Parameters:
      live - their hit rate on us since the last change
      baseline - their hit rate on us in the profile
      Returns:
      whether live is certainly the higher
